[CL4SRec](https://arxiv.org/html/2010.14395) randomly retains a contiguous subsequence, with length controlled by a crop ratio; its start need not preserve the latest interaction. Crop, mask and reorder operations generate paired views for a self-supervised contrastive loss alongside supervised next-item prediction. Cropping therefore teaches representation agreement rather than directly assigning the original next-item label to every crop. [DuoRec](https://arxiv.org/html/2110.05730) instead uses different dropout masks and retrieves sequences sharing the same next-item target as semantic positives. Its “supervised” component concerns contrastive positive selection; recommendation loss remains a separate objective. Recent-suffix cropping is not its defining augmentation.

For BERT4Rec, sequence segmentation already has precedent: the [original implementation](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data.py) includes sliding windows, repeated random masking and forced last-item masking. Subsequent [CBiT](https://arxiv.org/html/2208.03895) uses sliding windows for long histories, combines Cloze masks with dropout to construct multiple views, and jointly optimizes masked-item reconstruction and dynamically weighted contrastive loss. Sliding windows sample historical segments; retaining a variable-length recent suffix fixes the endpoint and varies only how much preceding context remains.

Cropping only endpoint masked-target examples is consequently best described as supervised context-length augmentation: for target y, retain a suffix of its preceding history, append [MASK], and optimize prediction of y. No representation-alignment objective, paired-view negatives or same-target retrieval is required. Apply cropping only to these examples while retaining ordinary masked-item training elsewhere; inference can still use all available history within model capacity plus an appended mask. Assessment: cropping itself and unchanged inference are established ideas. Any narrower novelty claim should concern the endpoint-only application, suffix-length distribution and interaction with ordinary Cloze training, supported by controlled ablations; these sources do not establish priority for that exact combination.
